cards.name: Vivid Light
cards.summary: Contrast mode from the Hard Light family that works per channel: where the layer's colour is lighter than 50% grey it Color Dodges the image below (brighter, lower contrast), where it is darker it Color Burns it (darker, higher contrast), and exact 50% grey leaves it unchanged, giving one of the harshest light modes: saturated, punchy colour with crushed shadows and blown highlights. On the blend plate the bar band is indistinguishable from Normal (0 / 100% bar channels burn to 0 or dodge to full); the grey ramp crushes the photo to black on its dark half and blows it to white on its light half, with the photo itself visible only near the centre; the bottom band is near-solid hot pink-red at the opaque magenta end, fading to the photo, and the white type stays white.
use_for: bold, saturated colour grade from a gradient or solid fill layer, usually with Opacity or Fill pulled well down
gritty, high-contrast texture or grunge overlay on poster and album-art photos
detail / clarity effect: duplicate a layer, invert it, set it to Vivid Light and blur it to get a high-pass-like layer for sharpening or skin work
aggressive dodge-and-burn on a neutral-grey layer when Overlay or Soft Light is too gentle
avoid: Saturated or near-black / near-white blend colours clip the image to flat colour at 100%: use Overlay or Soft Light for a gentle tint, or lower Opacity / Fill.
It is one of Photoshop's 'special eight' modes where Fill and Opacity give different results; lowering Fill keeps more of the harsh contrast than lowering Opacity, so try both.
Not offered in 32-bit/channel (HDR) documents, which only list a reduced set of modes; convert to 16-bit first.
Text and logos on a Vivid Light layer lose their own colour and become unreadable over busy photos; keep type in Normal mode.
cards.equivalents_note: No real match: Illustrator's blending modes and CorelDRAW's transparency merge modes (cdrMergeMode) have no Vivid Light. The nearest in look is Hard Light (AI: HARDLIGHT; CorelDRAW merge mode cdrMergeHardlight), which is much softer because it uses Screen/Multiply instead of Dodge/Burn.
pairs_with: layer Opacity and Fill sliders (Fill behaves differently in this mode)
Blending Options > Blend If sliders to protect shadows or highlights
Gradient Map or Solid Color fill layers for colour grading
Invert + Gaussian Blur / Surface Blur on a duplicate layer (high-pass-style detail)
Hard Mix (the thresholded version of Vivid Light) and Linear Light (its linear sibling: Linear Dodge / Linear Burn instead of Color Dodge / Color Burn)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); var r = new ActionReference(); r.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID('layer'), stringIDToTypeID('ordinal'), stringIDToTypeID('targetEnum')); d.putReference(stringIDToTypeID('null'), r); var l = new ActionDescriptor(); l.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID('mode'), stringIDToTypeID('blendMode'), stringIDToTypeID('vividLight')); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID('to'), stringIDToTypeID('layer'), l); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('set'), d, DialogModes.NO);  // DOM: layer.blendMode = BlendMode.VIVIDLIGHT; works on pixel layers and layer groups
cards.cost: none while editing: a live layer property, switch back to Normal any time; Merge / Flatten bakes the result, and exporting to formats without layers flattens it

review.changes: summary: 'the harshest of the light modes' softened to 'one of the harshest' (Hard Mix is harsher); plate description corrected: the grey ramp does not clip to pure primaries (Vivid Light against the gradient leaves it a blue-washed band: blue at full, one channel near 128, the other swept 0-255), the black strip and dark areas go deep blue across most of the width, white type and hairlines stay white (computed per channel from the plate's colours); use_for: removed the invented '10-40%' opacity range; pairs_with: Linear Light is not uniformly 'gentler' (it lifts shadows harder at moderate blend values), now described as the linear sibling. Checked and kept: AM set call and DOM BlendMode.VIVIDLIGHT match the invoke; no Vivid Light in AI blend modes or CDR cdrMergeMode (pgd.py items), HARDLIGHT / cdrMergeHardlight exist as the nearest look; 32-bit limit confirmed against Adobe's 32-bit blend-mode list (Vivid Light absent)

verified.note: Frame matches Color Burn / Color Dodge with 2 layer, composited by the layer's alpha from the top layer and the photo plate and downsampled like the gallery, within 0.48 levels mean (99th percentile 2) in the worst band. The plate sentence described the earlier full-frame magenta-to-cyan gradient plate and was rewritten from this frame (bars, ramp, fading band).

second_opinion.note: The frame equals the formula composite, so it shows the mode itself; the only fault was the plate sentence, written for the earlier full-frame gradient plate. Re-sampled the rewritten claims (8 bar centres, 5 ramp points, 5 bottom-band points, the white type and hairline pixels) against blend_samples and they hold; no person in the photo is described.
